intent: A horizontal rule between two sections of options in a SelectContent.
typical_uses: A break between two captioned groups of options

dont_use_when.situation: A rule between sections of a page or a card, outside any select

invariants.text: select.module.css pulls the rule out by the list's padding on both sides, so it runs edge to edge across the popup, and gives it vertical margin of its own.
select.module.css draws only a horizontal rule; `orientation` changes the announced `aria-orientation`, not the drawing.
The separator renders with role `separator`, takes no pointer events and is not an option that arrow keys land on.

anti_patterns.dont: Put a separator first or last in the popup, or two in a row
anti_patterns.do_instead: Place separators only between options or groups; a rule at an edge or doubled draws a break with nothing on one side

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: A general Separator used inside the popup
bad.why: The popup accepts SelectSeparator, whose margins are set against the list's padding; a general Separator stops short of the popup's edges.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SeparatorState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.
